Several hundred lithium fluoride detectors of various types were produced for the measurements, including highly sensitive LiF:Mg,Cu,P (MCP-N) and standard LiF:Mg,Ti (MTS-N) detectors.
The MCP detectors have a much higher sensitivity compared to the MTS detectors, with a detection threshold below 1 μGy and the ability to measure doses up to 1 MGy.
Pairs of 6LiF/7LiF detectors were used to distinguish between the neutron and non-neutron components of the radiation field.
Sixteen cylindrical polyethylene (PE-300) moderators were used to detect higher energy neutrons.
The TLD measurements were calibrated in terms of neutron fluence using calibration data from the PTB Thermal Neutron Reference Field at GeNF.
The neutron fluence varied over more than four orders of magnitude, from around 10^4 n/cm^2 in the labyrinth to over 10^12 n/cm^2 near the tokamak.
The MTS detectors showed higher measured doses compared to the MCP detectors due to their higher efficiency for detecting high-LET radiation like thermal neutrons.
The MCNP simulations generally underestimated the measurements in positions close to the machine and overestimated them in positions far from the machine.
The background neutron fluence was estimated to be around 5x10^5 n/cm^2 for the dosimeters stored in the J1D lab and about half that for the ones in the office.
The experiences gained from this study will provide a firm basis for implementing TLD technology for area radiation monitoring at ITER to minimize personnel dose.
A total of 1.21x10^18 neutrons were produced by JET plasmas during the two-week exposure period.
The MCP detectors have a linear-sublinear dose response, while the MTS detectors have a linear-supralinear response.
The 6Li-enriched detectors showed a higher dispersion in their measurements due to self-shielding effects.
The largest discrepancies between the MCNP simulations and measurements were found for the 6Li-enriched TLDs, which have the largest self-shielding effect.
The orientation of the TLD cylinders with respect to the neutron source was not recorded, which contributed to uncertainties in the shielding and shadowing effects.
